name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,528

clue.text: Totter's tip - "Play cards and pray"

indicators.note: to play with something is to fiddle about with it, so the words that follow get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rag-and-bone man's motto: deal the cards and hope for the best.
explanation.walkthrough: A totter is a rag-and-bone man, a scrap collector who once went door to door with a cart; a tip is a dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap collector's dump is the yard where old metal and junk are stored and sorted.

clue.text: Film Swedish manager touring Spain

indicators.note: someone touring a country travels all around it, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: Sven-Göran Eriksson, the Swedish football manager
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A Swedish football boss travels round Spain, perhaps for a documentary.
explanation.walkthrough: Sven-Göran Eriksson managed England's football team; E is Spain's car registration letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Se7en is the 1995 David Fincher thriller starring Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman.

clue.text: Communist has to hide missing nationalist in overhaul

indicators.note: missing means going without, so one letter is dropped from the word for hiding

blocks.note: red is the traditional colour, and nickname, of a communist
to envelop something is to wrap it up out of sight
N is a standard abbreviation for nationalist

explanation.surface: A party member must cover up the absence of a nationalist during a reorganisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To redevelop a site or district is to rebuild and renovate it thoroughly, giving it a full overhaul.

clue.text: Instrument to stretch out the rank and file

blocks.note: to protract is to prolong or draw out
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A device for drawing out the ordinary soldiers, as if mustering troops.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the military term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is a geometry tool for measuring and drawing angles, a classic school drawing instrument.

clue.text: Old Anglo-Norman church holds single part of the bible

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside, so one piece sits within the church abbreviation

blocks.note: AN is the abbreviation for Anglo-Norman
CE is the Church of England
I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: An old Norman church houses a lone fragment of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient describes something belonging to the distant past, a straightforward synonym for very aged.

clue.text: Grimmest earl arrested by Tudors in revolt

indicators.note: someone arrested by police is held in custody, so this letter is held inside the rest
a revolt overturns the established order, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historical scene: an earl seized by the Tudor dynasty during an uprising, with grim results.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tudors were the royal house that ruled England from 1485 to 1603.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour means stern and gloomy, so the dourest person is the most sombre and severe, the grimmest.

clue.text: Passage in left part of church

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: A corridor running down the left-hand side of a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks architectural, like an aisle, but it means a passage of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse of time is an interval or period that passes, as in after a lapse of several years.

clue.text: Allows Westside gang leader to change

indicators.note: the first letter of the gang's name is swapped for a different letter

blocks.note: the Jets are one of the rival gangs in West Side Story

explanation.surface: A gang permits its boss to be replaced, in a musical turf war.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the J of JETS to L to get LETS; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone do something is to permit it, so lets is a direct synonym for permits.

clue.text: Picture instruction to reader to embrace prostitute

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms round someone, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page for the reader
ho is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A racy image with a note telling the viewer to hug a streetwalker.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a picture taken with a camera, so the two words are interchangeable.

clue.text: Melt ham and nearly new processed cheese

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
processed food has been broken down and reshaped, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A recipe: melt some ham and a nearly fresh slice of processed cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese with large holes, much used for melting in fondues and toasties.

clue.text: Record travelling back in canoe with divers

indicators.note: travelling back means going the opposite way, so the letters are read from right to left
only the letters lying in the words at the join are used, not the whole words

blocks.note: the tail end of this word
the opening of this word

explanation.surface: Filming a canoe trip back upstream with a team of scuba divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' tells you to put canoe and divers side by side; read the letters at the join backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To video something is to record it on camera, so the verb record is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Reportedly heard no-good ostler in trial venue

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so we want a word that sounds like another
no-good tells us to remove the G, the abbreviation for good

blocks.note: to catch a remark is to hear it; in British speech caught and court sound the same
an ostler looks after horses at an inn, as a groom does

explanation.surface: A useless stable hand was apparently overheard while at his trial.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British accents caught and court are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom is the chamber where a judge hears cases, the place where a trial is held.

clue.text: Tyneside author extremely short gets credit facility

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter of the preceding word goes

blocks.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
Jules Verne, the French science-fiction writer
very means extremely

explanation.surface: A Geordie writer who is very short of money takes out a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: The never-never is British slang for hire purchase, buying goods on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Hire purchase is nicknamed this because the payments seem to go on for ever, a form of credit buying.

clue.text: Complete beginner returns for gift

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a noob is slang for a total novice, especially in gaming

explanation.surface: A total novice comes back to collect a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something welcome that is given, close to a present or godsend.

clue.text: The French footing drinks bill for meeting

indicators.note: footing means standing at the foot, so in this down clue that piece goes at the bottom

blocks.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
a tab is a bill run up at a bar
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French friends paying the bar bill for a get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-table discussion is a meeting where participants confer as equals, like Arthur's knights.

clue.text: Jazz fan behind push to get American skunk

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the jazz fan follows the other piece

blocks.note: to pole a punt is to push it along
cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A jazz lover gives a shove from behind and lands an American skunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push' looks like a verb of shoving someone, but it is to pole, as with a punt.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the name polecat is applied loosely to skunks, smelly mammals of the same broad family.

clue.text: Cover heads of old Ukrainian ladies in essential oil

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, so we keep only those

blocks.note: a patch covers a hole or an eye
the initials of these three words
the first letter of this short word

explanation.surface: Babushkas in Ukraine wrap their heads in scarves, smelling of fragrant oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads of old, Ukrainian, ladies and in give O, U, L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is a heavily scented aromatic oil from an Asian plant, used in perfume and aromatherapy.

clue.text: Excessive hint about award

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

blocks.note: a touch of something is a hint or trace of it
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone suggests that a prize is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is an honour in the personal gift of the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Too much means more than is needed or reasonable, so it is a phrase meaning over the top.

clue.text: True Incan sacrificed in the lap of the gods

definitions.text: in the lap of the gods

indicators.note: something sacrificed is destroyed, so the original letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A faithful Inca is offered up to the gods in a sacrificial ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: The Incas did practise human sacrifice, which makes the surface fit the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: If an outcome is in the lap of the gods it is beyond human control and unpredictable, so not settled.

clue.text: Dancing with North African around bar

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: tap is a style of dancing
a Moor is a North African of Berber or Arab descent

explanation.surface: Someone dancing with a North African partner circling the pub floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it turns the second word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the room in a pub or inn where beer is served from the tap, a bar.

clue.text: Switzerland intervening in state's political organisation

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: CH, for Confoederatio Helvetica, is Switzerland's code
Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: Swiss neutrality meets meddling in another nation's party politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A political machine is a party organisation that controls votes and patronage, like Tammany Hall.

clue.text: Pointed article removed from official

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, so those letters disappear

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
canonical means officially authorised

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued newspaper piece gets withdrawn by a bureaucrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed' suggests a cutting remark, but here it is the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone tapers to a point, so a conical shape is one that comes to a tip, pointed.

clue.text: Goes over religious symbols

blocks.note: first meaning: travels across, as over a road
second meaning: Christian emblems of the crucifixion

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for traversing a bridge or street and a plural noun for Christian emblems.

clue.text: Champion in the rotunda

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A winner stands beneath a domed hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is someone who wins or defends a cause, and a hero is a celebrated, admired figure of courage.

clue.text: Portrait artist eats Indian food

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside it, so the words hold the letters wanted

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A painter of portraits enjoys a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a cooling yoghurt side dish with cucumber or mint, served with curries in South Asian cuisine.

clue.text: Trump's dressed in tailored timelessly cute red coat

indicators.note: timelessly means without time, whose abbreviation T is taken away
tailored clothes are cut and reshaped, so these letters are refashioned

blocks.note: taken as written, then one T removed

explanation.surface: A president dons a smart, sweet red coat made to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump's signals the American spelling, -ER rather than British -RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be accoutred is to be kitted out or attired; the US spelling suits an American president.

clue.text: Capital of Germany with a king and a queen

blocks.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
taken as written
K is king in chess notation
taken as written
R is for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Berlin hosts a royal couple, a king and a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Germany' looks like one phrase meaning Berlin; Capital alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dakar is the capital city of Senegal, on the westernmost point of the African mainland.

clue.text: Notes occasion

blocks.note: two notes of the sol-fa scale, ti and me, a variant of mi

explanation.surface: Someone jots notes about an event.
explanation.walkthrough: Ti and me (also spelt mi) are both sol-fa notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A time is a particular instance or event, as in the last time we met, so it means occasion.

clue.text: Pieces of software for gas and electricity companies?

blocks.note: first meaning: small programs that do housekeeping tasks on a computer
second meaning: firms supplying public services such as power and water

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both helper programs on a computer and the public service providers for power, water and heating.

clue.text: Learner welcomed by second chess player

indicators.note: someone welcomed by a host is taken in, so this letter goes inside the other word

blocks.note: L is for learner, as on L-plates
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: A novice is greeted by the runner-up at a chess tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a runner-up or a moment, but it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess one side plays the dark pieces, and that player is named after their colour.

clue.text: Picture of Kairos with Melchior?

blocks.note: Kairos is the setter, who refers to themselves as I
Melchior is traditionally one of the three Magi, the wise men

explanation.surface: A nativity snapshot of the setter alongside one of the wise men.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in the clue stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a visual representation such as a painting or photograph, a direct synonym for a picture.

clue.text: Festival regularly endears resident of New Jersey?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: Easter is a Christian festival
the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A spring holiday regularly makes someone from New Jersey more lovable.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: New Jersey is on the US East Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the eastern United States, such as New Jersey, is called this by other Americans.
